text:
ana: FYI ap-south1 rack-r4 started failing provisioning after today's BMC firmware 1.2.9 -> 1.2.10 push. GPUs show stuck in provisioning, serial consoles drop, secureboot bit flipped on some nodes. logs below.

mike: ack, can you paste the error from the manager?

ana: paste: `watchdog: bmc_reboot_request(0x3) at 03:12:11` then `ipmi: session closed (conn reset)`

devon: seeing NVMe detach and `kexec: starting new kernel` in dmesg on 3 nodes, likely BMC watchdog triggering hard reset mid-provision. Repro on canary node-r4-02.

infra-bot: deploy/firmware/1736504321 failed on 12/120 hosts (job id: deploy-1736504321). auto-rollback: NOT_TRIGGERED (policy: manual).

jules: is secureboot toggle expected? that should be preserved. if toggled, images won't boot. :thinking_face:

ana: looks like Nuvoton BMC toggles `SecureBootEnable` when it fails to write flags during watchdog reset. My plan: drain affected ASG, mark nodes `fw:rollback-patch`, roll back BMC to 1.2.9 on 3 canaries then validate provisioning. If that fails, warm-swap capacity to us-west-2 with buffer 20% — but note reserved capacity mismatch and egress/cross-region costs.

mike: +1. estimate of cost delta?

ana: rough calc: 20% of 500 GPUs moved => 100 GPUs; using on-demand warmup plus cross-region egress ~ $30k/week extra while we reprovision. Also SLA risk due to rack affinity for some customers.

devon: runbook steps:
1) tag nodes: `kubectl label node node-123 fw=rollback20260319`
2) `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS raw 0x2e 0x01`  # vendor rollback index
3) monitor `dmesg | grep -i kexec` and `journalctl -u provisioner` for 10m

ana: starting canary roll now: node-r4-02 -> rollback -> reprovision. I'll update thread. @sre-oncall please prepare capacity plan in us-west-2 if canary fails.

sre-oncall: will queue capacity request and estimate cost. prepping warm pool and cross-region egress estimates. bookmarking runbook. :thumbsup:

ana: update 1736504600: canary rollback succeeded, provisioning completed, secureboot preserved. rolling to remaining 11 affected nodes during off-peak window 02:00 UTC. leaving this thread open for post-mortem notes.
